audits.claim: Deleting cached data leaves the displayed cache status stale when the wrapper has no onChanged callback.
audits.evidence: packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-384 renders the wrapper without onChanged; the wrapper forwards that absent callback at packages/platform/atoms/selected-calendars/wrappers/SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:183 and :75. With an owned Google credential containing cached rows, deleteCache.handler.ts:28-32 deletes them, but CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42-50 only shows a toast and invokes the optional callback, with no invalidation. The wrapper query disables focus refetch at :159, and the menu continues rendering the old cacheUpdatedAt through CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:69-82; packages/trpc/react/trpc.ts:100-125 supplies no global mutation invalidation.

audits.claim: Running the webhook helper from the repository root targets the parent directory's .env instead of the repository's .env.
audits.evidence: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5 assigns the relative path ../.env and never changes directory. Invoking ./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root with a successfully obtained tunnel URL therefore creates or modifies the parent's .env at :62-70, leaving the intended repository configuration unchanged (.env.example:150 declares GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL). GoogleCalendarService reads that variable for webhook addresses at packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:40-42 and :159, so the helper can report success without configuring the application.

audits.claim: The connected-calendars status query bypasses the global calendar-cache flag and can display stored rows while caching is disabled.
audits.evidence: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.ts:22-28 substitutes the mock when the global flag is disabled, and calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27-30 would return no status. Instead connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-35 directly creates the real repository, whose calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-186 query reads retained rows regardless of that flag. This proves the bypass, but displaying and allowing cleanup of actually stored data does not itself enable caching or produce incorrect availability; the repository contains no contract requiring management status to disappear when caching is disabled.

audits.claim: The migration labels legacy cache rows with the migration time rather than their previous cache write time and contains a contradictory warning.
audits.evidence: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:3 says there is no default, whereas :9 adds NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), initializing existing rows to the migration time. connectedCalendars.handler.ts:29-35 exposes the maximum of this new column and CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:88-92 labels it Last updated, so an untouched legacy row initially has an approximate timestamp. Availability validity still uses expiresAt in calendar-cache.repository.ts:112 and :127, and new writes refresh expiresAt at :161/:168; the impact is transitional display accuracy and misleading migration documentation, not cache correctness. Recovering historical times by subtracting today's 30-day constant would additionally require verifying historical writers.

audits.claim: The delete handler accesses Prisma directly rather than using the calendar-cache repository abstraction.
audits.evidence: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:17-30 checks ownership and directly deletes rows through prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany. calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts:7-33 exposes no delete method, and the real calendar-cache.repository.ts:51-189 has none, although calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:23-25 has an unused deleteManyByCredential stub. This is an abstraction consistency concern with no demonstrated functional failure; CalendarCache.init at calendar-cache.ts:22-28 would indeed return a no-op mock when disabled, so routing deletion through it without changing that behavior would be inappropriate.

audits.claim: The new cache deletion ownership boundary and status query have no targeted tests.
audits.evidence: The checkout's tests contain no references to deleteCacheHandler, getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, or connectedCalendarsHandler; the calendars router directory contains only setDestinationCalendar.handler.test.ts. packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.test.ts:30 and :111 cover the existing getCachedAvailability and upsertCachedAvailability methods, but not the new grouping query at calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-186. The new ownership guard at deleteCache.handler.ts:17-26 is implemented, so absent regression tests are a coverage concern rather than proof that foreign credentials can be deleted.

audits.claim: The features package imports @calcom/platform-constants without declaring it as a dependency.
audits.evidence: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:6 adds the platform-constants import, while packages/features/package.json:9-33 contains neither a dependency nor a development dependency for it. packages/platform/constants/package.json:2 defines the workspace package, and yarn.lock contains its workspace resolution, so this is not a nonexistent module. The configured node-modules linker (.yarnrc.yml:1) permits workspace hoisting; no current runtime failure is established, but declaring the direct dependency would make the package manifest accurate.

audits.claim: The new dev:cron command uses an undeclared, unpinned tsx executable through npx.
audits.evidence: apps/web/package.json:11 replaces the declared ts-node runner with npx tsx cron-tester.ts, while :196 still declares ts-node. No package manifest or yarn.lock entry supplies tsx, so the repository no longer pins or installs this runner. That introduces an external installation/version dependency on an uncached development machine, but no concrete incompatibility is established; the finding's claim that npx downloads it on every run also overstates the problem because npx can reuse its cache.

audits.claim: The webhook helper can reuse a stale log URL belonging to a different Tunnelmole session.
audits.evidence: Suppose a previous helper session left https://old.tunnelmole.net in /tmp/tmole.log, and a new tmole 3000 process was started manually with output elsewhere. scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:8 and :28-31 detect the new process but extract the first URL from the old fixed log via :23-24; only the branch that starts its own process clears the log at :34. Because the stale URL is nonempty it passes :55-59 and is appended to an env file without an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL at :70, then reported as current at :73. When that configuration is loaded, CalendarService.ts:40-42 and :159 use the stale host as the webhook callback address, preventing callbacks from reaching the current local tunnel.
